papers.title_en: EMODE: Dynamic Para-Semantic Experts for Emotion-Aware Speech Language Modeling
papers.authors: Jianan Pan, Yiwen Gu, Xinze Li, Rui Wang, Kejie Huang
papers.evidence: 情感感知语音语言模型，分离副语言与语义两条通路
papers.tldr: 大型语音语言模型擅长跨模态理解与生成，却难以保留副语言线索，尤其是情感。EMODE 提出动态副语义专家 DPSE，将连续语音特征分解为语义与副语言路径，动态路由并在送入语言模型前融合。采用语义预热、副语言激活、联合精炼三阶段课程，并配合 OEG、SAA、GDR 约束。在 SER、共情回复及双语 MEPA 基准上，EMODE 更好平衡词汇保真与情感敏感度，增强情感接地生成，凸显显式副语义分解对跨语料情感理解的价值。
papers.abstract_en: Large speech language models have demonstrated strong capabilities in unified cross-modal understanding and generation, yet paralinguistic cues, especially emotion, remain difficult to preserve. Existing systems typically rely on entangled acoustic representations, which allow the underlying language model to depend excessively on recovered lexical content instead of grounding its behavior in acoustic-prosodic evidence. We address this limitation with EMODE, an emotion-aware speech language model built around \textbf{Dynamic Para-Semantic Experts (DPSE)}. DPSE decomposes continuous speech features into semantic and paralinguistic pathways, routes them dynamically, and fuses them before integration into the language model. To turn this structural decomposition into functional specialization, EMODE is trained with a three-stage curriculum consisting of semantic warm-up, paralinguistic activation, and joint refinement, guided by Orthogonal Expert Guidance (OEG), Semantic-to-Acoustic Alignment (SAA), and Gating Diversity Regularization (GDR). Experiments on SER test, empathetic response evaluation, and the newly constructed bilingual MEPA benchmark show that EMODE improves the balance between lexical fidelity and emotional sensitivity, strengthens affect-grounded response generation, and exposes the value of explicit para-semantic factorization for robust cross-corpus emotion understanding.

papers.title_en: AccentCL: Robust Accent Classification with Incremental Expansion
papers.authors: Mu-Ruei Tseng, Waris Quamer, Ghady Nasrallah, Ricardo Gutierrez-Osuna
papers.evidence: 语音分类中跨语料域偏移与域均值对齐损失
papers.tldr: 现有口音分类器标签集固定，难以在新增数据时扩展新口音，且跨语料常存在类别不平衡与域偏移。AccentCL 从冻结的 Whisper-Large-v3 提取多层表征，用不平衡感知交叉熵和域均值对齐训练，并通过回放式持续学习与新旧类边界损失扩展标签空间。五类任务达 77.1% 平衡准确率、76.9% 宏 F1；加入西班牙口音新类 F1 为 83.3%，基类保持 77.3%；再加入中文口音新类 F1 为 61.8%，旧类保持 77.6%。结果表明无需全量重训即可稳健地增量扩展口音类别。
papers.abstract_en: Accent classifiers are typically trained with a fixed label inventory and cannot accommodate new accent categories as new data becomes available. Moreover, accented speech corpora often exhibit substantial class imbalance and/or domain shift due to differences in recording conditions across corpora. We present AccentCL, a class-incremental learning framework for English accent classification that is robust to class imbalance and cross-corpus domain shift. AccentCL extracts multi-layer representations from a frozen Whisper-Large-v3 encoder, optimized with an imbalance-aware cross-entropy loss to reduce bias toward the majority accent classes and a domain mean alignment loss that minimizes distributional mean shift across training corpora. The label space is then expanded via replay-based continual learning, using the frozen base model for knowledge retention and an old-to-new margin loss to reduce overprediction on newly added classes. On a five-class accent classification task, AccentCL achieves 77.1% balanced accuracy and a 76.9% macro-averaged F1 score. We further evaluate the model's ability to incrementally incorporate two new accent categories: Spanish-accented and Chinese-accented English. When adding Spanish-accented English to the pretrained model, AccentCL attains an F1 of 83.3% on the new class while retaining 77.3% balanced accuracy on the base classes. When subsequently adding Chinese-accented English, it achieves 61.8% F1 on the new class while preserving 77.6% balanced accuracy on the previously learned classes. These results show that AccentCL enables robust regional accent classification while allowing new accent categories to be added without full retraining.

papers.title_en: A Comprehensive Benchmark of Source-Free Universal Domain Adaptation on Time Series Representations
papers.authors: Romain Mussard, Fannia Pacheco, Maxime Berar, Paul Honeine, Gilles Gasso
papers.evidence: 无源通用域适应基准，处理标签集不匹配与域偏移
papers.tldr: 源数据不可访问、标签集又不匹配的源自由通用域适应（SF-UniDA）在图像领域渐受关注，但时间序列尚无基准且难度更高。本文构建了首个时间序列 SF-UniDA 基准，并首次系统评测预训练基础模型作为特征提取器的表现。研究发现所有现有方法对拒绝未知样本的推理阈值高度敏感，为此提出可插拔的自动阈值模块。在三个时间序列数据集上的实验验证了该模块的有效性，并揭示基础模型并未系统性优于经典骨干网络。
papers.abstract_en: Source-Free Universal Domain Adaptation (SF-UniDA) extends Universal Domain Adaptation by removing access to source data at adaptation time while still handling label-set mismatches between domains. Despite growing interest in this setting for image data, no benchmark exists for time series, which are more challenging. We present the first SF-UniDA benchmark on time series. In addition, we provide the first study of pretrained foundation models as feature extractors for time series domain adaptation. In this context, we identify a critical and previously underexplored limitation of all existing SF-UniDA methods: the inference threshold for unknown-sample rejection is highly sensitive. We address this by proposing a plug-in auto-thresholding module that can be integrated into any SF-UniDA method. Experiments on three well-known time series datasets confirm the suitability of this module. They also highlight that foundation models do not systematically outperform classical backbones and that SF-UniDA tailored for time series is yet to be developed.

papers.title_en: Batched Speech Decisions Without Decoding: Single-Token Supervision Lets a Frozen LLM Hear Beyond the Transcript
papers.authors: Jie Jin, Ziyin Ma, Min Yin, Jinyu Chen, Haigang Song, Zhikun Pang, Xiaowen Zhang
papers.evidence: 冻结LLM经连接器从语音读取情感
papers.tldr: 全双工语音代理需频繁做小规模封闭决策，现有系统依赖慢速自回归解码，难以满足实时性。提出DuplexJev，将ASR编码器隐状态经小连接器送入冻结LLM，把每个问题读作选项上的单token分布，无需解码，并以读出答案token的交叉熵训练。8-GPU节点约0.1秒完成8条语音的80个决策；末层连接器下口语QA达90%（文本91%）；交叉注意力连接器下性别与情感准确率均达90%（原55%和28%），口语QA仅降1点。发布权重、训练配方、批推理流水线及双语口语QA集。
papers.abstract_en: Full-duplex voice agents make many small, closed decisions, which current systems answer by slow autoregressive decoding. We propose DuplexJev, which feeds ASR-encoder hidden states through a small connector into a frozen LLM and reads each question as a single-token distribution over its options. Nothing is decoded, and an 8-GPU node answers 80 decisions about eight utterances in about 0.1 s. With a last-layer connector, spoken QA stays close to reading the transcript (90% vs. 91%). DuplexJev also hears the speaker: gender and emotion accuracy both reach 90% (from 55% and 28%) with a cross-attention connector, whose spoken QA drops by only 1 point (83% to 82%). We train decisions with cross-entropy on the read-out answer token, instead of the usual transcript distillation, whose teacher never hears the voice, and keep distillation for content. Encoders and LLMs are interchangeable; we release weights, training recipe, a batched-inference pipeline for full-duplex serving and a bilingual spoken-QA set.

papers.title_en: SkillFormer: Skill-Decomposed Adaptation for Audio Language Models
papers.authors: Lee Seung-woo, Bowen Qi, Kim Min-jun, Jang Won-young
papers.evidence: 音频语言模型的技能分解适配，涵盖情感识别
papers.tldr: 音频语言模型需掌握音高比较、说话人计数、节奏估计、情感识别等数十种技能，但联合训练易相互干扰，一项提升常以另一项退化为代价。SkillFormer 把音频理解分解为技能专属低秩适配器，推理时由路由器根据问题动态选择并加权组合。训练采用交替调度：先按技能簇更新各适配器，再联合校准路由器，以缓解梯度冲突。它仅增加不到4%参数，在MMSU、MMAU-Pro、MMAR三种架构模型上平均准确率提升2.5至4.1分，感知、推理和语义子类均均衡受益。
papers.abstract_en: Audio language models must handle dozens of distinct skills, from pitch comparison and speaker counting to musical tempo estimation and emotion recognition. Joint training on all skills at once causes interference: gains on one skill often come at the cost of another. We propose \textbf{SkillFormer}, which decomposes audio understanding into skill-specific low-rank adapters and composes them at inference time through a learned router. The router examines the question to decide which adapters to activate and how much weight each should carry, so that a pitch query engages different parameters than a genre classification query. An alternating training schedule updates each adapter on its own skill cluster before jointly calibrating the router, preventing the gradient conflicts that arise in standard multi-task optimization. SkillFormer adds fewer than 4\% of the base model's parameters and requires no changes to the audio encoder or language backbone. Evaluated on three architecturally distinct models across MMSU, MMAU-Pro, and MMAR, it raises the average accuracy by 2.5 to 4.1 points, with balanced gains across perception, reasoning, and semantic subcategories.
